original_question: Is it true that the set {t in R : F_x(t) = c} or the set {t in R : F_x(t) = omega}, whenever nonempty, must contain a Cantor set?
target_in_paper: The nearest official target is the cardinal-function open problem asking whether the continuum level set F_x^{-1}(𝔠), if nonempty, must contain a Cantor set; your draft's added mention of F_x^{-1}(ω) appears to mix this with the adjacent result that the combined infinite-fiber set F_x^{-1}({ω,𝔠}) is dense whenever some value has infinitely many representations. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00025-020-01260-x))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant object as a level set of the cardinal function, correctly singles out the two infinite cardinal values ω and 𝔠, and correctly focuses on the structural conclusion 'contains a Cantor set'. Those are exactly the nearby issues discussed in the cardinal-function literature around the survey. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00025-020-01260-x))
missing_details: The paper-context object x must be specified: x is a summable sequence generating an achievement set, not an arbitrary function or parameter. In the sequence-language used in recent cardinal-function papers, x is a non-empty sequence of positive real numbers with finite sum; in the earlier measure-language formulation of the same problem, the question is stated for an absolutely convergent series. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.13016))
F_x must be defined explicitly as the cardinal function on the achievement set A(x), namely F_x(t)=|{A⊆N : Σ_{n∈A} x_n = t}|, with values in N∪{ω,𝔠}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.13016))

The ambient set of t should be the achievement set A(x) (or equivalently one may write t∈R and allow empty fibers outside A(x)); the paper-faithful formulation is about fibers of the cardinal function, not arbitrary real level sets of an unrelated map. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.13016))

The nearest official open problem is about the 𝔠-level only. The ω-level is not asked in that same official formulation; instead, the neighboring proposition only proves density of F_x^{-1}({ω,𝔠}) under the weaker hypothesis that some point has infinitely many representations. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00025-020-01260-x))

The notion of 'Cantor set' should be made explicit as a subset homeomorphic to the standard Cantor set (the older paper phrases this in the equivalent compact perfect/dense-in-itself language for subsets of complete metric spaces). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00025-020-01260-x))

The draft omits the nontriviality assumptions implicit in the area: x should be an infinite summable sequence, since otherwise the level sets for ω or 𝔠 cannot occur. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.13016))
refined_question: Let x=(x_n) be a summable sequence of positive real numbers, let A(x)={Σ_{n=1}^∞ ε_n x_n : (ε_n)∈{0,1}^N} be its achievement set, and define the cardinal function F_x:A(x)→N∪{ω,𝔠} by F_x(t)=|{A⊆N : Σ_{n∈A} x_n=t}|. If F_x^{-1}(𝔠) is nonempty, must F_x^{-1}(𝔠) contain a Cantor set? ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00025-020-01260-x))
justification: The strongest paper-faithful correction is to drop the separate ω-level question. The closest recoverable official formulation in the cardinal-function line of work is exactly the continuum-level problem 'if f^{-1}(𝔠)≠∅, does f^{-1}(𝔠) contain a Cantor set?'; the neighboring statement about ω is only Proposition 2.8, which gives density of the union of the infinite levels F_x^{-1}({ω,𝔠}), not a Cantor-subset conclusion for F_x^{-1}(ω) itself. So your draft is close in theme but not exact in scope: it combines one open problem with a nearby contextual proposition. Because your notation uses F_x rather than f_μ, I rewrote the question in the standard sequence/achievement-set notation while keeping the problem no broader than the original intent. I could confirm the survey's existence and general purpose from the arXiv abstract page, but the exact in-survey page/label for this item was not retrievable in the accessible web view; the refined wording therefore follows the closest official recoverable formulation and its immediate context from the cited cardinal-function source. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17285))
